challenges.says: The story claims the action that enables the value name box only while delete-one-value is chosen (block-96284792383932228976, rule businessrule-30251051045932916641 in the step), yet none of its criteria states it; that behaviour is only covered in the second story, so the action is claimed twice or not covered here.

The second and third criteria (removed on the machine when applied; represented by the deletion entry rather than erased) have empty 'from' although businessrule-27194812132584860836 states exactly this, and the third largely restates the first.

'Taken from the selection without asking' comes from the inferred step change and not from any cited rule or decision, so it is behaviour the rule does not state and the criteria give no reason for it.

Most criteria (clear everything, clear first keeping ordinary values, loss of deletion entries and sub-key values, typed name accepted and replaced by a deletion entry, cancel or Escape changes nothing) have an empty 'from' although they are sentences of businessrule-63694206615951133419, so they are not traced to the rule they enforce.

The wording 'existing direct values with ordinary content' and 'sub-keys' is carried over from the rule and is hard for a product owner who never saw the code to follow; it should be put in plain words or defined as a term.

The title, 'what' and 'why' say the person is told what will go and that a value is removed after confirmation, but businessrule-04432638879352685329 only asks for confirmation when forgetting a key and says nothing of any confirmation or description for a value; the last criterion shows a value is forgotten with none.
The second, third and fourth criteria have empty 'from' although businessrule-04432638879352685329 states them, so they are not traced to the rule.
